 Judgment
This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- from respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are; That, on 27-10-2019 at about 7.45 p.m., petitioner was going towards Horamavu outer ring road from Vemana Circle, Banasawadi by riding Vespa Scooter,
bearing No.KA-05-JS-0434 along with her friend Ranu Bai as pillion rider, slowly, cautiously on correct side of road, when they reached opposite to Desi Masala Restaurant on Banasawadi 100 feet road, at that time driver of Toyota Etios Car, bearing No.KA-03-MQ-2767 came from opposite direction i.e., ring road side with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, lost control over his vehicle, went to its wrong side of the road and dashed against the petitioner's scooter.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took 3 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, she was studying in final year BDS (4th year) at Shyamala Reddy Dental College, Marathahalli, Bengaluru.
But, due to the accidental injuries, till today she is bed ridden and could not attend her classes.
Therefore, petitioner prayed for compensation.

3. In brief, the objections by respondent No.1 and 2 are that;
3(a).

In written statement of objections, respondent No.1 denied the petition averments generally and contended that the car, bearing No.KA- 03-MQ-2767 was insured with respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
He prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3(b) Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car, bearing No.KA-03- MQ-2767 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the other petition averments generally and it contended that the petitioner was riding the Vespa Scooter, bearing No.KA-05-JS-0434 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmet and without possessing valid vehicle documents in the rash and negligent manner with high speed and suffered self accident, the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the alleged accident, the driver of car was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of M.V. Act.
As without prejudice, it contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper party as the alleged driver of the insured vehicle is necessary party to the proceedings.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the M.V. Act.
For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:

sentences.text: 10. The spot mahazar and draft sketch depict the scene of occurrence.
The MVA report shows there was no mechanical defects in the vehicles to the incident.

The wound certificate reveals grievous injuries caused to the petitioner such as multiple small abrasions over right knee joint, multiple abrasions over right side of face, deformity on right hip noted, noted to have right 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 lip posterior dislocation.
The above said injuries on right hip are grievous in nature.
The accident was not due to the mechanical defects in the sense, then that could have been by the negligence only.
Now whose negligence was there to the incident to be analyzed.
No independent eyewitness is examined herein.
The petitioner herself is as good as the eyewitness.
As already noted the final report shows the negligence by the driver of the offended car.
As per the sketch and as admitted by the petitioner herself the incident was by head on collision.
The line of admission is extracted here as follows for better appreciation; " ".
So that it is clear that there was the rash and negligence by both vehicles, otherwise the incident could not have been occurred as averred or otherwise the things could have been different.
Admittedly the petitioner has seen the car from 50 feet prior to the incident.
Then in such a distance if both the petitioner and the driver of car tried to avoid or controlled their vehicles obviously there was every chance of avoiding the incident, but failed.
It is therefore from the scenario the negligence which was contributed by the petitioner to the incident cannot be ruled out.
Thus, it is found that the incident was due to the rash and negligence in riding and driving by both vehicles and such negligence could be assessed at 50:50 ratio.
Further, without here being contrary evidence, here is no impediment to believe the police 8 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 records.
Under the fact and circumstances of the case the final report stands partly accepted; thus, the police records stand considered.

11. Regarding objections by respondent No.2 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and the petitioners approached the Tribunal, respondent No.2 had already taken all the contentions of respondent No.1 the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act, and discussion on the same now does not arise.

12. Regarding objection of respondent No.2 of non joinder of necessary party is concerned as final report came to be filed against the offended car the parties already arrayed are suffice, however respondent No.2 didn't take suitable steps in the proper stage and the petitioner herself is the rider is taken to be considered.
13.

Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that the petitioner met with motor vehicle accident on 27.10.2019 at about 19.50 p.m., and sustained simple and grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Toyota Etios Car, bearing No.
KA-03- MQ-2767 and also due to the rash and negligence 9 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 riding by the petitioner.
Hence, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Income
As discussed on the head of avocation, the petitioner's avocation taken to be considered notionally i.e., Rs.20,000/- per month.
Considering the avocation and income notionally now loss of future income due to disability needs to be calculated.
According to the determined age of the petitioner multiplier is 17.
So, 12% of monthly notional income comes to Rs.2,400/- x 12 months x multiplier 17 = Rs.4,89,600/- it is considered as compensation under the head of loss of future income due to the disablement.
12 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 Laid up period and Pain and sufferings
Petitioner was treated as inpatient from 27-10- 2019 to 04-11-2019.
She suffered fracture.
So that, she suffered pains and sufferings and also lost medical education at the time of her treatment as well as her nourishment at least for the period of 4 months.
It is therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation considering his pains and sufferings and for her laid up period.

Hence, it is opined that 4 months' notional income of Rs.80,000/- + Rs.75,000/- for pains and sufferings = Rs.1,55,000/- will be just and proper in compensation for laid up period and pain and sufferings.
Medical Bills:
It is averred that petitioner spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards the medical expenses.
To prove the same, she produced 18 medical bills as per Ex.P13.
All those bills have been examined with care and caution and found that bill at serial No.3 is not in the name of the petitioner.
It is therefore, the amount mentioned in this bill cannot be considered.

Except this rest of the medical bills are considered; -
accordingly total amount of medical bills considerable is Rs.1,03,072/- for which the petitioners are entitled for.
Amenities and happiness:
It is established that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The assessment of disability by the 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 doctor and its consideration as discussed above are to be considered herein.
With such permanent disablement she will have to lead her future life.
From such injuries she suffered pains, difficulties, which deprived her of leading her happy life and from enjoying amenities.
It is therefore, the petitioner is entitle for compensation for loss of her such amenities and happiness.
So, It is deemed proper to award compensation of Rs.75,000/- under this head.
Food, Nourishment, Attendant charges and Conveyance:

Under the facts and circumstances of the case having considered the nature of the injuries and permanent disablement, though here is no document particularly, it could be presumed that the petitioner might have spent considerable amount for her nutritional food, nourishment, attendant charges and conveyance.
It is therefore, it is opined that for such food, nourishment, attendant charges and for conveyance is concerned awarding of Rs.30,000/- as compensation is just and proper.
Hence, it is considered so.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.
So, the petitioner is entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on 50% of compensation amount.

Liability:
17.
Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As 15 (SCCH-16) MVC 7861/2019 found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offending car and also on the part of the petitioner.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay part of compensation.
The petitioner is also liable for her part of negligence which should be borne by herself.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.2 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioner is only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.
